claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child - I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! And one more important question:

**Do you live with Alex, or are you responsible for him in terms of paying for his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute about £10 a week towards his upkeep - you know, helping with things like clothes and bits he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify a bit more about your contributions:

**Are you contributing at least as much as the Child Benefit payment amount? Currently, Child Benefit is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child, or £16.95 per week for additional children. You mentioned you contribute £10 per week - is this the total amount you contribute, or do you also provide other support such as buying clothes, giving pocket money, or making other payments for Alex's care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the £10 a week is what I contribute - that's the total amount I'm able to help with at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more important question:

**Who does Alex currently live with, and is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his mum - my ex-partner. I'm not sure if she's claiming Child Benefit for him or not.

conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

While Alex is 8 years old (meeting the age requirement of under 16) and you live in the UK, you don't currently live with Alex - he lives with his mother. 

To qualify for Child Benefit when you don't live with your child, you need to be contributing at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards their upkeep. The current Child Benefit rate for an eldest or only child is **£25.60 per week**. 

You mentioned you're contributing £10 per week, which is less than the required £25.60 threshold. This means you don't meet the financial contribution requirement to be considered responsible for Alex under the Child Benefit rules.

Additionally, only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child, and since Alex lives with his mother, she would typically be the person entitled to claim.

**Important to note:** Alex's mother may be eligible to claim Child Benefit if she hasn't already done so, as she lives with him and is his primary carer.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if Alex comes to live with you, or if you're able to increase your contributions to at least £25.60 per week - your eligibility could change.
